title: code-mode supersedes NARF; durable/scheduled cells removed; single V8 embedder
content: The bro-harness authorial/metatool surface is Codex-style "code-mode": the vendored crate `crates/bro-code-mode` plus the `exec` and `wait` tools in `crates/bro-harness/src/code_mode.rs`. The full filtered tool surface (builtins + capability tools + MCP) is projected into a cell as the typed `tools.*` namespace; a cell's nested `tools.X(...)` dispatches the same filtered tool the flat surface exposes (the deny policy is honored in-box, no bypass). This SUPERSEDES NARF, which is fully retired — `narf_exec/prepare/run/define/register/registerWorkflow/scheduleWorkflow`, `NarfSession`, and the whole box-edge invariant framing are removed. Durable/scheduled cells are also removed as half-baked: `crates/bro-script`, `src/cells.rs`, the `CellRegistryCapability`/`DurableCellCapability` traits in bro-capabilities, the `install_cells`/`install_durable_cells` hooks, and `ArtifactKind::Cell` are all deleted. INVARIANT: exactly one V8 embedder in the process — `bro-code-mode`; never reintroduce a second `v8::V8::initialize()` (two embedding crates poison the V8 platform init).
rationale: Worked through the original NARF box-edge invariant ("the box dereferences; never selects/reviews/launches") and concluded it was the wrong frame: an unenforceable runtime re-encoding of an epistemic intent, with per-tool in-box/out-box placement a category error (role lives in data flow, not the tool). Codex code-mode is the battle-tested conservative shape. Adopting it forced NARF removal because two crates cannot both initialize the V8 platform in one process (the combined harness test binary poisoned the init lock). Durable/scheduled cells were removed at operator direction as half-baked. Landed and validated: bro-code-mode 35 tests pass on v8 149; bro-harness 142 pass; daemon builds and its capabilities/artifacts/system_events tests pass.
